references.text: Moses blesses the tribes of Israel before his death, in the same way that Jacob gathers his sons to give them his farewell blessing.
A father's call for children to listen - 'Come, children, listen to me' - a thematic parallel to Jacob's words to his sons about gathering and listening.
Isaiah uses similar language: 'Hear this, house of Jacob, you who are called by the name of Israel' - a parallel to the use of both 'Jacob' and 'Israel' in the source verse.
Moses calls for listening in his farewell song, similarly to how Jacob calls his sons to listen in his farewell speech.
The list of Jacob's twelve sons who are now gathered to hear their father's final words in chapter 49.
Both verses establish God's authoritative speech to the entire nation by using 'house of Jacob/house of Israel' as a collective appeal.
